title: Jewelry worth millions of dollars stolen from French museum in daring early-morning raid
facts: Burglars stole millions of dollars worth of jewelry from the Lalique museum on Sunday, July 5, 2026.
The Lalique museum is located in the town of Wingen-sur-Moder in northeastern France.
The thieves broke into the Lalique museum around 5:30 am by forcing a door.
The burglars smashed open six display cases inside the Lalique museum's jewelry room.
Approximately twenty pieces of jewelry were stolen during the Lalique museum break-in.
The estimated value of the stolen Lalique museum jewelry is close to four million euros.
The jewelry stolen from the Lalique museum was made of crystal without any precious gems.
A cleaning lady was the first person to arrive on the scene and call the police after the Lalique museum burglary.
The Lalique museum originally opened in 2011 near the company's factory.
The Lalique museum houses over 650 works of Art Nouveau jewelry, Art Deco glass, and contemporary crystal.
The town of Wingen-sur-Moder has a population of approximately 1,500 inhabitants.
Thieves stole 102 million dollars worth of jewelry from the Louvre museum in Paris in October 2025.
A security audit revealed that 35% of the rooms in the Louvre's Denon Wing were not monitored by security cameras during the 2025 heist.
Thieves stole three porcelain works from the Adrien Dubouche National Museum in Limoges in September.
Four men smashed display cases at the Cognacq-Jay museum in Paris in November 2024 to steal 18th-century works.
